messages:
emma_support: Hey @channel — blocked ticket from AcmeCorp. Their Azure Marketplace invoice shows ~1.2M token charge for Mar 3 (invoice INV-9842) but our internal usage dashboard shows ~820k tokens for the same tenant and date. Customer is escalating, wants line-item evidence. Can someone pull the marketplace metering report and raw events?

jason_billing: Thanks Emma. Do we have the Marketplace customerId / tenant id to map? I can start by reconciling invoice items vs our aggregated usage.

emma_support: Tenant ID: tenant-acme-71, Azure MarketPlace subscription GUID: 4a2f-9b8d-e123. Customer says invoice line item SKU: AI-INFERENCE-STANDARD. Attaching the invoice screenshot they provided: https://redwood.internal/screencaps/inv_INV-9842.png

sophia_support: Adding context from the support ticket — customer reports spikes between 02:00-04:00 UTC and says they only ran a short load test. They attached a set of request_ids they captured: [req_3921, req_3922, req_3978].

liam_engineer: I'll check ingestion for azure_marketplace_metering events. Quick query I'm running:
```
SELECT event_time, metering_id, tokens, resource_id
FROM marketplace_metering
WHERE subscription_guid = '4a2f-9b8d-e123' AND DATE(event_time) = '2026-03-03'
ORDER BY event_time;
```

liam_engineer: Preliminary results: I see a burst of many small metering events around 02:15 UTC with identical request headers and duplicate metering_id patterns (metering-XXXX-dup). Could be duplicate ingestion from the partner connector.

jason_billing: If the marketplace pushed duplicate metering records, invoices could double-count unless Azure deduped. Do we have raw billing postback logs? @ops-bot can you surface the raw webhook delivery for that subscription on Mar 3?

ops-bot: Retrieved 78 webhook deliveries for subscription 4a2f-9b8d-e123 on 2026-03-03. First delivery: 2026-03-03T01:58:12Z. Last delivery: 2026-03-03T04:11:09Z. Logs: https://redwood.internal/ops/logs/webhook/4a2f-9b8d-e123/2026-03-03

liam_engineer: From the webhook payloads I pulled one example — looks like this:
```
{"metering_id":"metering-xx-123","tokens":1024,"request_id":"req_3921","timestamp":"2026-03-03T02:15:13Z"}
{"metering_id":"metering-xx-123","tokens":1024,"request_id":"req_3921","timestamp":"2026-03-03T02:15:14Z"}  # duplicate
```

liam_engineer: Two almost identical deliveries ~1s apart. Our ingestion pipeline should dedupe on metering_id but I see many with suffixes like `-dup` instead of exact match so dedupe missed them.

emma_support: Customer is pushing for a fix and refund if overcharged. What is the next step for us?

jason_billing: Steps: 1) Confirm total tokens from our canonical usage table (dedup by normalized metering_id) 2) Compare to invoice line items and compute delta 3) If delta > 0, propose credit and submit incident to Azure partner channel. I can handle the accounting once Liam confirms canonical totals.

liam_engineer: Canonical tokens after aggressive dedupe (strip -dup suffix + dedupe on request_id) for the date = 814,732 tokens. Raw marketplace events sum = 1,216,488 tokens. Delta = 401,756 tokens (~49% overcount).

sophia_support: Noted. Customer wants a written reconciliation they can forward to Azure. Can we produce CSV with both sets of events and flags for duplicates?

liam_engineer: Yes. I'll export two CSVs: raw_webhooks_4a2f-9b8d-e123_20260303.csv and reconciled_usage_4a2f-9b8d-e123_20260303.csv and put them in the secure share. Expect in ~30m.

alex_partner: Looping in Azure Marketplace partner ops — can you confirm whether Azure sends dedup hints or if duplicates can reach us? Also confirm if marketplace billing dedup occurs on their side.

ops-bot: Uploads created: /secure-share/raw_webhooks_4a2f-9b8d-e123_20260303.csv (78 rows), /secure-share/reconciled_usage_4a2f-9b8d-e123_20260303.csv (42 rows). Links: https://redwood.internal/secure-share/4a2f-9b8d-e123/mar03

jason_billing: I'll draft a reconciliation email to AcmeCorp and cc Azure partner ops with the CSVs and proposed credit. Emma, can you confirm ticket language and customer time expectations?

emma_support: Yes — customer asked for resolution within 48h. I'll reply with provisional findings and the CSVs once Jason reviews. Also flagged for refunds team. :eyes:

liam_engineer: Root cause hypothesis: partner connector had retry logic that appended `-dup` to metering_id on retries, bypassing our dedupe. Fix: normalize metering_id on ingest (remove suffix pattern) and add request_id dedupe. I'll open an eng ticket and patch the ingestion lambda.

jason_billing: Filed billing adjustment request. Ticket BIL-2026-332 with preliminary credit of ~401,756 token units. Will update after accounting validation.

emma_support: Thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated and move to pending-resolution.

sophia_support: Customer reply: "Thanks for the quick investigation — we'll wait for the reconciliation and credit." :+1:

liam_engineer: Quick follow-up: rolling patch to ingestion normalized ids scheduled for 2026-03-05 03:00 UTC with a short maintenance window. Will monitor telemetry post-deploy.

jason_billing: Closing loop: once patch is live, we should run retro for other partners and search for `-dup` patterns across last 90 days.

emma_support: Good plan. Closing thread in support once credit issued.
